title.value: Multi-XScience: A Large-scale Dataset for Extreme Multi-document Summarization of Scientific Articles
title.justification: The title is clearly listed at the beginning of the paper, reflecting the main contribution, which is the Multi-XScience dataset designed for multi-document summarization.
title.quote: Multi-XScience: A Large-scale Dataset for Extreme Multi-document Summarization of Scientific Articles

analysis.description: The paper introduces Multi-XScience, a large-scale multi-document summarization dataset from scientific articles. The dataset aims to assist in the task of writing related-work sections of papers based on their abstracts and referenced articles. It emphasizes the utility of abstractive models given the high level of text abstractiveness in its summarization task.

type.justification: The paper involves the creation of a large-scale dataset and conducts empirical tests with several state-of-the-art summarization models to validate its utility and challenge.
type.quote: Descriptive statistics and empirical results—using several state-of-the-art models trained on the Multi-XScience dataset—reveal that Multi-XScience is well suited for abstractive models.

name.justification: The paper is focused on summarization, a key area within Natural Language Processing, particularly dealing with multi-document summarization tasks.
name.quote: Multi-document summarization is a challenging task for which there exists little large-scale datasets.

name.justification: The core task discussed in the paper is summarization, specifically multi-document summarization, which is clearly a subfield of NLP.
name.quote: We propose Multi-XScience, a large-scale multi-document summarization dataset created from scientific articles.

name.justification: Pointer-Generator is mentioned as a model utilized in the evaluation of the dataset.
name.quote: Pointer-Generator incorporates attention over source texts as a copy mechanism to aid the generation.

is_contributed.justification: Pointer-Generator is referenced as a pre-existing model used for testing the dataset, not a novel contribution of this paper.
is_contributed.quote: In addition, we apply existing state-of-the-art single-document summarization models, including Pointer-Generator (See et al., 2017)

is_executed.justification: The paper reports empirical results using the Pointer-Generator model, indicating it was executed as part of their tests.
is_executed.quote: When comparing abstractive models to extractive ones, we first observe that almost all abstractive models outperform the unsupervised extractive models—TextRank and LexRank—by wide margins.

is_compared.justification: Pointer-Generator's performance is compared to other models in terms of abstractive summarization achieved on the dataset.
is_compared.quote: To our surprise, Pointer-Generator outperforms self-pretrained abstractive summarization models, such as BART and BertABS.
